messages:
Noah Patel: Heads-up FinFlow sent our renewal. They've introduced a new 'latency-tier' SKU and bumped the per-embedding rate.
Lucia Vega: ouch, paste the quote lines?
Noah Patel: pasted below:
```
FinFlow Renewal 2026
- Enterprise base: $21,750/mo
- Latency-tier (new) : $2,900/mo
- Embedding unit      : $0.0032 per embed (was $0.0021)
- Renewal discount    : none quoted (term: 12 months)
```
Tom Rivera: I recall we had a 12m commit with a 12% renewal concession last year. @billing-bot can you confirm contract and last net invoice?
billing-bot: Contract FF-RED-2025: committed ARR $252,000; renewal credit 12% applied. Net invoiced (2025) = $221,760.
Lucia Vega: That delta looks big. Can someone run the expected spend if we accept as-is? Quick calc: (21,750 + 2,900) * 12 = $296,400 annual vs net last year $221,760 -> ~34% increase.
Noah Patel: Agreed. Action items: Procurement to push for reinstated renewal discount or multi-year price lock; Finance to export month-by-month embedding counts for last 9 months; Ops to ask FinFlow for line-item definition and telemetry behind 'latency-tier'.
Tom Rivera: Also request a data export showing counts billed under any latency metric for the past 12 months. We need to see if we're actually using it.
Lucia Vega: Can someone draft the vendor email? I'd like us to ask for a 45-day pricing hold instead of the standard 30 so we have time to model tail usage.
Noah Patel: I'll draft. Posting draft for edits before sending:
```
Subject: FinFlow  renewal questions, usage tieout, and pricing hold request

Hi FinFlow team,

We received the renewal for FF-RED-2026 and need clarification before we can proceed. Please provide the following:
1) Line-item definition and billing metric for the new "latency-tier" SKU, and any telemetry/usage that would cause billing under that tier over the last 12 months.
2) Monthly embedding API usage for the last 9 months (counts per month) and a CSV export suitable for our finance model.
3) Confirmation of any available renewal discounts for 12- or 24-month commitments, or a 2-year price lock option.
4) Please place the quoted pricing on a 45-day hold while we reconcile usage and evaluate pricing options.

If the latency-tier is mandatory, please propose a trial period (3 months no charge) or a phased ramp with credits to limit near-term cost impact.

We will not approve any auto-renewal that includes the latency-tier without explicit written acceptance from Redwood.

Thanks,
Noah Patel
On behalf of Redwood Inference
```
Tom Rivera: Add a line asking them to confirm whether this change is due to a product feature (new telemetry) or a licensing/packaging change. That affects our negotiation stance.
Noah Patel: Added. Sending later today, cc procurement@redwood and billing.
Lucia Vega: @billing-bot please attach contract FF-RED-2025 and invoice_2025-12 to this internal thread for reference.
billing-bot: Attached: contract_FF-RED-2025.pdf, invoice_2025-12.pdf :white_check_mark:
Tom Rivera: Negotiation targets: reinstate 12% + remove latency-tier, or keep latency-tier but apply 20% off total for the term. If they push back, propose 24-month price lock at 15% off.
Noah Patel: Good. Also flag: do not allow auto-charge of new SKU at renewal. Explicit opt-in required.
Lucia Vega: I'll start the embedding usage pull and share the CSV here. If the usage shows minimal hits to latency-tier we can push for waiver.
Noah Patel: Appreciate the quick response team. Will post FinFlow reply when received. :thumbsup:
